conflicts.point: Whether automated continuous integration and ninety-day audit cycles can replace common law tort oversight without compromising public safety.

positions.stance: Dynamic escrow pools and automated audit logs provide faster, more reliable restitution and error correction than slow tort lawsuits.
Replacing tort oversight with automated administrative compliance mechanisms removes vital legal deterrents and externalizes catastrophic risk.

conflicts.point: Whether pre-deployment causal validation must serve as a mandatory regulatory gate before deploying high-stakes algorithms.

positions.stance: Independent pre-deployment causal audits must be mandatory to prevent encoding historical bias into black-box systems.
Pre-deployment administrative gating freezes technological progress and perpetuates higher baseline error rates from human decision-makers.

verdicts.conflict: Whether automated continuous integration and ninety-day audit cycles can replace common law tort oversight without compromising public safety.
verdicts.rationale: The debate lacks comparative empirical data across both software engineering and the legal system. Both positions operate on incompatible frameworks for measuring safety and harm.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Long-term comparative data tracking error rates and victim compensation outcomes across hospitals using continuous audit logs versus those operating under traditional tort liability.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-deployment causal validation must serve as a mandatory regulatory gate before deploying high-stakes algorithms.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position provides a concrete regulatory mechanism, whereas the accelerationist position relies on abstract claims about innovation speed. This makes the skeptic framework more actionable for legislative drafting.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Demonstrated evidence that post-deployment monitoring catches and corrects severe algorithmic bias faster and more reliably than pre-deployment gates.
